source.title: Tunneling the Loss Landscape: Bypassing Memorization with Monte Carlo Parameter Swapping
source.authors: Lai-Shun Chan; Xiaotian Zhang; Yue Shang; Ge Zhang; Entao Yang

page_placements.theme: Delayed generalization depends on training conditions

record.file_problem: The full paper text is present. PDF extraction has minor formatting artifacts, but no material section appears cut off.
record.tranche_reason: Measures the training-to-test generalization delay in a modular arithmetic grokking task and reports how parameter perturbations change it, extending the study of delayed generalization to this setting. It does not test the listed versions’ specific architecture, optimizer, batch-size, regularization, model-width, sharpness, or example-removal claims.
record.gate_note: Results on grokking time and on parameter mobility, replica correlation, and trajectory fractal dimension are recorded. Cited prior work and hyperparameter-selection statements are not rows. The study does not test random-label fitting or the listed versions’ interventions and comparisons.
record.test_reason: The study measures delayed generalization and training dynamics in modular arithmetic transformers. None of its results tests V1–V8: memorization here means fitting structured training examples, not random labels, and parameter mobility, replica correlation, and trajectory geometry do not measure magnitude-aware sharpness. The random-label finding is cited as background.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors interpret their diagnostics as evidence of glass-like kinetic arrest and report that swaps and other perturbations can accelerate generalization through increased exploration. They acknowledge that FD is local and window-dependent and that transfer beyond this modular arithmetic task remains unclear.
record.recipe_differences: Studies modular arithmetic grokking with a 1-layer transformer, Adam/AdamW, probes, Gaussian noise, and parameter swapping; it does not reproduce the original random-label/generalization experiments or the listed version tests.
record.method_sensitivity: Waiting time changes replica correlation. Perturbation method changes generalization timing. Swap ratio affects training stability and timing; the text reports r = 10−2 as most stable and fastest, with smaller ratios recovering baseline grokking and larger ratios tending to induce excessive fluctuations. FD estimates depend on the fixed 20-epoch window and sampling choices.

fits_no_version.finding: Training accuracy reaches 99% before test accuracy; parameter swapping advances generalization onset to approximately epoch 650 versus epoch 3000 for AdamW.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: FD-triggered parameter swapping can shorten delayed generalization in a modular arithmetic transformer.

fits_no_version.finding: Parameter mobility declines, replica correlation depends on waiting time, and local trajectory fractal dimension approaches 1 during memorization before increasing after generalization.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Modular arithmetic grokking exhibits slow, history-dependent and geometrically constrained training dynamics.

fits_no_version.finding: Adam with large Gaussian parameter noise and Adam with swaps generalize earlier than the small-noise Adam probe baseline.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Parameter perturbations can accelerate generalization onset in modular arithmetic grokking.

record.problems: The experiments are limited to modular arithmetic grokking with a 1-layer transformer. The authors say generalization beyond this task and extension to realistic vision or language models remain unclear. FD is estimated with a fixed local 20-epoch window and is sensitive to sampling choices. Error bars are omitted in the plots; variability from large perturbations is acknowledged. No random-label capability check is reported.
record.rows_left_out: No additional eligible results identified beyond the extracted measurements and intervention outcomes.

untested.parts: Joint demonstration of random-label fitting, natural-label generalization, and chance-level held-out performance with random labels.
Test-error changes when width increases beyond the width required for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and the contribution of local connectivity or initialization.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under limited or broader tuning, including recovery through optimizer modifications.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and recipes that reduce large-batch penalties.
Dropout's effect on held-out error and its dependence on training-set size, strength, augmentation, or weight decay.
Magnitude-aware sharpness ranking generalization gaps among comparably fitted convolutional networks and comparison with norm- and margin-based measures.
Test-accuracy changes after removing highly memorized training examples versus equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: States of cannot_determine refer to the listed claim versions, not denial of the reported grokking findings. No version-specific verdict is warranted.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting and held-out performance under random labels are not tested.
No width sweep or comparison beyond the interpolation threshold.
No convolutional versus fully connected image-classifier comparison.
No comparison of adaptive optimizers with SGD on the listed benchmarks.
No batch-size comparison or fixed-epoch large-batch penalty test.
No magnitude-aware sharpness measurement or comparison with norm- and margin-based measures.
No removal of memorized examples or retraining comparison.

rows.subject: 1-layer transformer
rows.operation_detail: Measured parameter displacement (PM) during AdamW training.
rows.measure: Parameter mobility, dR; the text reports it dropping from ∼ 1 to ∼ 10−2 between t ≈ 0 − 102 and toward ∼ 10−4 by the end of training.
rows.value: ∼ 1 to ∼ 10−2 between t ≈ 0 − 102; toward ∼ 10−4 by the end of training
rows.locator: Observation, Parameter Mobility and Slow Relaxation; Figure 1b
rows.note: The authors say mobility becomes vanishingly small around t ≈ 104; this is a measurement during grokking, not a test of the listed sharpness measure.
rows.check: Parameter mobility does not measure any listed version. It is net parameter displacement over a 20-epoch window, averaged across layers, rather than one-step displacement.

rows.subject: 1-layer transformer
rows.operation_detail: Measured replica correlation for replicas branched at tw = 0 under small Gaussian perturbations.
rows.measure: Replica correlation (RC): initial decorrelation, a plateau during grokking, then a marked decrease coinciding with generalization.
rows.value: Two-step relaxation; plateau followed by marked decrease
rows.locator: Observation, Two-step Relaxation of Replica Correlation; Figure 1c
rows.note: Reported as averaged across replica pairs, layers, and independent runs.
rows.check: Replica correlation measures similarity between perturbed training trajectories, not magnitude-scaled tolerance of weight perturbations before training error rises.

rows.subject: 1-layer transformer
rows.operation_detail: Compared replica correlation across waiting times.
rows.measure: Replica correlation as a function of waiting time; later-branched replicas remain near q ≈ 1 for an extended period and show only a minor later decrease.
rows.value: For larger waiting times (e.g. tw = 102, 103), correlation remains close to q ≈ 1 over an extended period before only a minor decrease.
rows.locator: Observation, Aging Behavior in Training Dynamics; Figure 1c
rows.note: Reported waiting-time dependence is evidence of history dependence in this task.
rows.check: Waiting-time dependence of replica correlation tests aging of training dynamics, not any listed version.

rows.subject: 1-layer transformer
rows.operation_detail: Estimated trajectory fractal dimension during AdamW training.
rows.measure: Trajectory FD: after training accuracy reaches 99%, FD collapses toward 1; after a prolonged period at 1, it gradually increases.
rows.value: FD collapses toward 1, then gradually increases
rows.locator: Observation, Dynamical Transition in Trajectory Geometry; Figure 1d
rows.note: Authors interpret FD near 1 as channel-like motion. They note that the estimator is local and window-dependent.
rows.check: Local trajectory fractal dimension does not measure any listed version, including V7's sharpness–generalization-gap relationship.

rows.subject: 1-layer transformer
rows.operation_detail: Applied state-aware parameter swaps after the FD threshold was reached, with loss-cap rejection.
rows.measure: Grokking time, defined as the period after training accuracy reaches 99% and before test accuracy reaches 99%.
rows.baseline: approximately t ≈ 3000 epochs for the AdamW model
rows.locator: State-Aware Monte Carlo Parameter Swapping (SAM-Swap); Figure 2a
rows.note: The text describes the swap intervention as substantially reducing the delay.
rows.check: This is the proposed method's performance, not evidence for V1–V8. Figure 2 identifies the swap condition as Adam+Swap, so assigning AdamW and weight decay 0.1 to that condition is unsupported. Approximately 650 and 3000 are epochs of generalization onset; the text does not establish these as durations measured from 99% training accuracy.

source_check.correct: Generalization onset occurs at approximately epoch 650 for Adam+SAM-Swap versus epoch 3000 for AdamW. These are reported training epochs, not explicitly quantified intervals between the training-accuracy and test-accuracy thresholds. Adam+Swap uses learning rate 10−2; weight decay 10−1 belongs to AdamW. Swap ratio 10−2, FD threshold 1.1, and rejection above the initial training loss are supported.
source_check.locator_found: Methods, lines 151–158; SAM-Swap, lines 326–358; Comparing perturbation methods, lines 420–435; Figure 2 caption, lines 444–454.
source_check.problem: The row misidentifies the swap optimizer as AdamW, assigns its comparator's weight decay, and presents onset epochs as threshold-to-threshold durations; this method comparison is not claim evidence.

rows.subject: 1-layer transformer
rows.operation_detail: Added Gaussian noise to all parameters as an intervention.
rows.measure: Test accuracy timing; the setting reaches generalization earlier than the baseline Adam probe setting.
rows.baseline: Adam probe, which uses σ = 10−5; exact grokking time not stated
rows.value: Earlier generalization than baseline; exact grokking time not stated
rows.uncertainty: Variability acknowledged; error bars omitted in plots
rows.note: The text reports earlier generalization but gives no exact time for this condition.
rows.check: An intervention comparator for generalization timing, not a listed-version result. Earlier generalization is explicitly reported; lacking an exact time does not make that finding partial.

rows.subject: 1-layer transformer

rows.measure: Test accuracy timing; the setting reaches generalization earlier than the baseline Adam probe setting.

rows.value: Earlier generalization than baseline; exact grokking time not stated
rows.uncertainty: Variability acknowledged; error bars omitted in plots
rows.note: The exact swap-model time is separately reported for the AdamW model in R5.
rows.check: The proposed method's performance should not be a claim-evidence row. This appears to duplicate R5's Adam+Swap condition. Earlier generalization is explicitly reported; missing numerical timing does not make it partial.

source_check.correct: Adam+SAM-Swap generalizes earlier than Adam with the weak Gaussian probe, σ = 10−5; that comparison has no numerical baseline timing stated. The SAM-Swap section separately reports approximate onset at epoch 650 for the swap intervention, versus epoch 3000 for AdamW.
source_check.locator_found: Small Additive Gaussian Noise as Probe, lines 244–252; SAM-Swap, lines 356–358; Comparing perturbation methods, lines 420–435; Figure 2 caption, lines 444–454.
source_check.problem: The qualitative comparison is supported, but the note incorrectly attributes the swap condition to AdamW. This overlaps R5's intervention and should not serve as evidence for V1–V8.

relation.reason: The introduction discusses random-label memorization and generalization, but the experiments do not compare random and natural labels or test any other listed version.

tranche.reason: The study measures modular-arithmetic grokking dynamics and intervention performance. It neither tests V1–V8 nor uses those specific findings as an experimental tool.

source_check.notes: The authors' conclusion paraphrase is supported. Results concern one modular-arithmetic transformer setup; FD is local and window-dependent, and transfer to other tasks or realistic models remains untested.
